overview: Oil eased for a second session on Tuesday as Monday's peace talks in Tehran — attended by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan — offered the first diplomatic channel in months, with the four nations agreeing to continue negotiations on preventing further military escalation. Brent crude dipped 0.6% to $115.15, extending its retreat from Friday's six-month high of $116.72, while WTI slipped to $101.32. The diplomatic push came as the Washington Institute for Near East Policy reported October was the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz since it began tracking incidents in 2017. Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi East-West pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport; the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three drones. US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fell to 282.6 million barrels — the lowest since October 1982 — leaving minimal buffer against any further supply shock. Newcastle coal eased 0.6% to $149.75 as IEA head Fatih Birol said he does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027.

Gold stabilised near $4,010 on Tuesday, recovering from Monday's early dip below $4,000 as the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.98% — its first drop below 5% in weeks. Markets now price roughly a 90% chance the Fed holds rates steady at Wednesday's FOMC decision, down from 37% for a hike earlier this month. Silver held at $53.96, platinum slipped to $1,529, and palladium edged up to $1,046. Copper firmed 0.5% to $6.54 per pound but remains well below its September record of $6.85. Grains fell across the board at Monday's close: wheat dropped 9 cents to $6.16, soybeans slid 15¼ cents to $12.41, and corn eased 1 cent to $4.55. Chinese lithium carbonate spot dropped below the key 100,000 yuan level for the first time, with futures at about 94,000 yuan. Bitcoin held near $80,050 ahead of the Fed decision, with Bitfinex identifying $77,000–$77,765 as the next support zone.

watchItems.title: FOMC decision, Wed Oct 28
watchItems.text: The Fed announces its rate decision Wednesday with Brent at $115, the 10-year yield at 4.98%, and the dollar firm. Markets now price roughly a 90% chance of a hold, down from 37% for a hike earlier this month, after several Fed officials tempered expectations. A hold with hawkish guidance could still weigh on gold and risk assets. The key question is whether the statement acknowledges the risk that oil-driven inflation becomes entrenched or signals the bar for a hike has risen.

watchItems.title: Iran peace talks gain traction
watchItems.text: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan held talks in Tehran on Monday — the first multilateral diplomatic push in months — and agreed to continue negotiations on peace and security. Oil fell from $116.72 to $115 on the news. But October saw the worst month for shipping attacks near Hormuz since 2017, Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi pipeline infrastructure the same day, and Iran fired a cruise missile at vessels it called rogue. Markets watching whether diplomacy translates into fewer attacks or merely a pause.

watchItems.title: US SPR hits 40-year low at 282.6M barrels
watchItems.text: Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fell to 282.6 million barrels — the lowest since October 1982. This limits the administration's ability to release oil to cool prices if Hormuz escalation worsens or if the reported post-midterms Iran strike scenario materialises. Combined with effective OPEC+ spare capacity at just 270,000 bpd, any confirmed supply disruption has almost no buffer. Russian refiners are increasing diesel output in October after the Kremlin granted export quotas following a US supply agreement.

watchItems.title: Lithium breaches ¥100,000 for first time
watchItems.text: Chinese lithium carbonate spot dropped below the psychologically important 100,000 yuan per tonne level for the first time, with futures falling to about 94,000 yuan — roughly halved from May's peak above 200,000 yuan. Goldman Sachs projects a global surplus by 2028. SMM expects a trading range of 90,000–110,000 yuan next week. But Q3 destocking slowed and LFP battery production is rising, so some analysts see limited near-term downside from here.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold stabilised near $4,010 on Tuesday, recovering from Monday's early dip below $4,000 as the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.98% — its first drop below 5% in weeks. December futures settled Monday up 0.8% at $4,038.40. Markets now price roughly a 90% chance the Fed holds rates at Wednesday's FOMC, down from 37% for a hike earlier this month. Gold remains about 28% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver held at $53.96, little changed on Tuesday as the metal tracked gold's stabilisation above $4,000. December futures settled at about $54.04. Silver is still down about 14% on the month, tracking one of its worst monthly performances of the year. The gold-silver ratio held near 74.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent eased 0.6% to $115.15 on Tuesday, extending its retreat from Friday's $116.72 six-month high. Monday's settlement came in at $115.81 after the market fell more than $2 intraday on peace talks in Tehran before recovering. WTI slipped to $101.32. Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi pipeline pumping stations, and October is the worst month for Gulf shipping attacks since 2017. US SPR crude stocks fell to 282.6 million barrels — the lowest since October 1982. Libya's Hamada–Tahara pipeline remains shut.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper firmed 0.5% to $6.54 per pound on Tuesday, bouncing from multi-week lows but remaining well below its September all-time high of $6.85. Concerns about AI-sector headwinds and uncertainty over US tariffs on refined copper imports continue to weigh on sentiment. Trading Economics models project $6.59 by year-end.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal eased 0.6% to $149.75 as the broader energy complex softened on Middle East peace hopes. The benchmark remains up 40% year-to-date as the Hormuz gas shock drives Asian and European utilities back to coal. IEA head Fatih Birol said he does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027. The IEA forecasts record global coal demand of 8.94 billion tonnes this year. Indonesia, the largest exporter, cut its production target with August shipments 23% below last year.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum slipped to $1,529 on Tuesday, down about 12% on the month as elevated yields and a firm dollar kept pressure on the PGM complex. The WPIC's forecast of an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year continues to weigh on sentiment.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium edged up to $1,046 on Tuesday, finding modest support but remaining near its lowest levels since mid-2025. The metal is down about 22% on the month. Auto-driven demand continues to weaken as platinum substitution in gasoline catalysts accelerates and battery-electric vehicle market share grows.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: ~30 transits/day vs 85 pre-war · worst Oct for attacks
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis deepened as the Washington Institute for Near East Policy reported October was the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping since it began tracking incidents in 2017. INTERTANKO reports US-facilitated transits exceeding 30 per day, still far below the pre-war baseline of 85. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan held peace talks in Tehran on Monday — the first multilateral diplomatic push in months — but Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi pipeline infrastructure the same day. US SPR crude stocks at a 40-year low of 282.6 million barrels leave minimal buffer against further disruption.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn settled 1 cent lower at $4.55 on Monday, pressured by continued harvest and fund liquidation. The US corn harvest remains near the five-year average pace. Managed money continues to hold substantial short positions in corn.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: December wheat dropped 9 cents to $6.16 on Monday, its largest daily decline in over a week. Managed money holds its largest net short position in wheat. Winter wheat planting is advancing on schedule and export demand remains subdued.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans fell 15¼ cents to $12.41¼ on Monday, hitting a two-month low as harvest pressure intensified. The US harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average, pointing to a record crop. Brazilian election uncertainty added a bearish undertone for trade flows.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin held near $80,050 on Tuesday, down 0.2% as crypto markets remained cautious ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision. The weekend low of $79,250 tested the $80,000 floor. Bitfinex sees $77,000–$77,765 as the next major support zone, with $81,300 now acting as resistance. Ethereum slipped to $2,323. US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows on October 22, reversing three days of inflows, as oil-driven inflation fears kept sentiment subdued.

desk.name: LNG
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) remains near $30 per MMBtu, with the latest weekly data from LNG Insights showing $29.77 as of October 19. Hormuz disruption continues to threaten Qatar's 106 million tonnes of annual export capacity, and QatarEnergy remains under force majeure. European TTF rose to approximately €97 per MWh. Henry Hub sits at $3.04, widening the gap with global spot markets and underscoring how disconnected US gas prices remain from the international crisis.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.sum: Sulfur prices remain elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,100–1,300 a tonne. Middle East FOB prices sit at $765 (Kuwait) and $740 (Qatar). China imported 56% of its sulfur from the Middle East pre-war, and Hormuz disruption continues squeezing sulfuric acid supply — the essential input for copper leaching, phosphate fertilizer, and oil refining. Domestic China sulfur trades near 7,200 yuan a tonne.

desk.name: Potash
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367.50 a tonne, down from $396.50 in July, as the market stays well supplied. China's 2025 contract settled at $348 a tonne. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions, routing through non-aligned buyers.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: Flat w/w · off 105k high · demand weak
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) stabilised near 90,000 yuan a tonne for the week of October 19–26 — the first flat week after two weeks of declines from the post-holiday high of 105,000 yuan. SMM describes a wait-and-see consolidation phase with low-level sideways trading expected. Smelter operating rates are low, raw material tightness has eased after September ore arrivals nearly doubled, and demand from flame retardant and PV glass sectors remains subdued. September antimony ore imports surged 92% month-on-month.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.sum: Gallium remains at a record $1,850 a kilogram outside China, up over 200% since early 2025. Beijing's Document No. 46 export controls set a presumption of denial for gallium exports to US end users. The Busan truce's Document No. 72 suspended that presumption for one year but Chinese exports have not meaningfully resumed. China produces about 98% of global gallium and 60% of germanium. Western recycling and new mines in Canada and Japan are years from meaningful output.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) averaged about $5.02 a pound in 2025, slipping from $5.44 in 2024 as steel demand softened. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage — cheaper per cycle than lithium-ion at 4+ hour durations. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply. A single large VRFB order can move the market.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.sum: ICE cocoa held near $5,600 a tonne as of October 23, consolidating after pulling back from its August 31 high of $6,821. The price is still far above the 1977 high of $5,104 and roughly double the March 2026 low of $2,846. Ivory Coast arrivals have improved sharply — up 19.8% in the current marketing year — and ICE inventories climbed to a 2.25-year high. However, forecasts for a strong El Niño affecting West African producers into 2027 keep the downside limited.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.sum: LME cobalt traded at $56,290 a tonne as of October 25, roughly steady. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes a year to support prices. The EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP is structurally reducing cobalt demand, but aerospace and superalloy uses provide a floor.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate spot dropped below the key 100,000 yuan level for the first time, with battery-grade spot at 99,350 yuan a tonne as of October 22 — down 2.7% week-on-week. Futures fell to 94,180 yuan, roughly halved from the mid-May peak above 200,000 yuan. SMM expects a trading range of 90,000–110,000 yuan next week. Goldman Sachs projects the global market flipping from a 404,000-tonne deficit in 2026 to a 444,000-tonne surplus by 2028. Spot prices stabilised and rebounded slightly on October 26.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades around $2,400 a tonne ($2.40/kg), firming on tight supply from Southeast Asia where Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia produce 70% of the world's latex. Fungal leaf blight (Pestalotiopsis) continues to reduce yields across the region. Auto-sector demand remains solid, and tyre makers are rebuilding inventories after destocking in 2024.
